module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 82

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 82](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.82)
- [An improved lower bound for a problem of Littlewood on the zeros of cosine polynomials](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16075) (Bedert, 2025)
- [Cosine polynomials with few zeros](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.01695) (Juškevičius & Sahasrabudhe, 2020)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real Set
open scoped Finset

namespace Green82

/-- The minimum number of zeros in $[0,1)$ of $\sum_{a \in A} \cos(2\pi a\theta)$
over all sets $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ of size $n$. -/
noncomputable def minZeros (n : ℕ+) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ A : {A : Finset ℤ // A.card = n},
    ({θ : ℝ | θ ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ ∑ a ∈ A.val, cos (2 * π * a * θ) = 0} : Set ℝ).ncard

/-- Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ be a set of size $n$. For how many $\theta \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$
must we have $\sum_{a \in A} \cos(2\pi a\theta) = 0$? The answer is the function `minZeros`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 42]
theorem green_82 : (answer(sorry) : ℕ+ → ℕ∞) = minZeros := by
  sorry

/-- Lower bound: every set has at least $(\log \log n)^{1-o(1)}$ zeros. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 42]
theorem green_82_lower_bound :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n →
        (⌊(Real.log (Real.log n)) ^ (1 - |o n|)⌋₊ : ℕ∞) ≤
        ({θ : ℝ | θ ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ ∑ a ∈ A, cos (2 * π * a * θ) = 0} : Set ℝ).ncard := by
  sorry

/-- Upper bound: there exists $A$ with at most $C(n \log n)^{2/3}$ zeros. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 42]
theorem green_82_upper_bound :
    ∃ C > 0, ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n ∧
      ({θ : ℝ | θ ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ ∑ a ∈ A, cos (2 * π * a * θ) = 0} : Set ℝ).ncard ≤
      (⌊C * (n * Real.log n) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)⌋₊ : ℕ∞) := by
  sorry

end Green82

reformulations.difference: The Lean states ⌊(log log n)^(1 - |o n|)⌋₊ ≤ #zeros (a floor and an absolute value on o), for every A : Finset ℤ with |A| = n. Green and Bedert say 'at least (log log n)^{1-o(1)} zeros', and Bedert's headline theorem is for sets of non-negative integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) Floor and |o|: I proved in Lean, in both directions, that the file's statement is equivalent to '∃ o → 0, ∀ᶠ n, ∀ A with |A| = n, (log log n)^(1 - o n) ≤ #zeros(A)'. Forward: keep the same o; since log log n ≥ 1 eventually, the power is monotone in the exponent, and ⌊x⌋₊ ≤ x. Converse: take o' = |o| + log 2 / log(log log n) → 0; then (log log n)^(1 - o') = x/2 ≤ x - 1 < ⌊x⌋₊ ≤ #zeros once x = (log log n)^(1-|o|) ≥ 2. (2) A ⊂ ℤ rather than ℕ: pairing a with -a (cos is even) turns f_A into Σ_b c_b cos(bt) with c_b ∈ {0,1,2} and g(0) = n. Bedert's Theorem 1.3 (any finite S ⊂ ℤ; here S = {0,1,2}, M(S) = 2) gives Z(g) ≥ c' log log n / log log log n = (log log n)^{1-o(1)}. His proof bounds the number of sign changes in (0,π) (the companion polynomial is built from them), and that number is at most the number of distinct zeros. So the file's count of distinct zeros is covered.

reformulations.difference: The Lean states #zeros ≤ ⌊C (n log n)^(2/3)⌋₊ (floor, cast to ℕ∞), for every n ≥ 1, with A : Finset ℤ. Juškevičius-Sahasrabudhe take A ⊆ ℕ and state O((n log n)^{2/3}).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since #zeros is a natural number, #zeros ≤ ⌊Y⌋₊ ⟺ #zeros ≤ Y for Y ≥ 0 (proved in Lean via Nat.le_floor_iff). J-S Theorem 1.1 is proved for all sufficiently large N, and the constant C absorbs finitely many small n ≥ 2, where (n log n)^{2/3} > 1. At n = 1 the right-hand side is ⌊C·0⌋₊ = 0, and A = {0} (no zeros) satisfies it (checked in Lean). J-S's sets lie in ℕ ⊂ ℤ, so the existential over Finset ℤ follows. Counting distinct zeros in [0,1) gives at most J-S's count of zeros in [0,2π], since f_A(0) = n ≠ 0.

reformulations.difference: Green writes Σ_{a∈A} cos(aθ) with θ ∈ ℝ/ℤ, which is literally ill-defined (cos(a(θ+1)) ≠ cos(aθ)). The Lean counts θ ∈ Ico 0 1 with Σ cos(2π a θ) = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only well-defined reading of Green's question is the count of zeros over one period. The substitution t = 2πθ is a bijection from [0,1) onto [0,2π), carrying zeros of θ ↦ Σ cos(2π a θ) to zeros of t ↦ Σ cos(at), which is the count in Littlewood's Problem 22 ('real zeros ... in a period'). [0,1) is a fundamental domain of ℝ/ℤ, so the Lean counts distinct points of ℝ/ℤ, as Green's 'for how many θ ∈ ℝ/ℤ' asks. For nonempty A the sum equals |A| ≠ 0 at θ = 0, so the zero set is finite and ncard is the true count, never the infinite-set junk value 0.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf (Problem 82 and its comments, pp. 38-39; PDF version dated 2026-01-30; text extracted from the content streams)
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2407.16075 (Bedert, LaTeX source: Problem 1.1, Theorems 1.2-1.4, Proposition 3.1, Section 4 companion-polynomial construction, Section 5 proof)

https://arxiv.org/e-print/2005.01695 (Juškevičius-Sahasrabudhe, LaTeX source: Theorem 1.1 'For each n in N there exists A ⊆ N, |A| = n, with Z(f_A) = O((n log n)^{2/3})', and Section 6 proof for all sufficiently large N)
review.notes:
No defects found. What was checked:

(1) Domain of A. Green poses Problem 82 for A ⊂ ℤ. This matches Littlewood's literal 'integral and all different', as quoted by Juškevičius-Sahasrabudhe. Bedert and J-S use non-negative integers. The file follows Green. Over ℤ, pairing a with -a gives coefficients in {0,1,2}, so the exact minima of the ℤ and ℕ versions could in principle differ. The known bounds are the same for both: the lower bound via Bedert's Theorem 1.3 with S = {0,1,2}, the upper bound because ℕ ⊂ ℤ. So the solved variants are correct as stated.

(2) Boundary cases. The ℕ+ domain of minZeros excludes n = 0, where the empty sum is identically 0 and ncard of the infinite zero set would be the junk value 0. I proved minZeros 1 = 0 in Lean (witness A = {0}). This is correct for Green's ℤ version: {a} with a ≠ 0 has 2|a| zeros, {0} has none. I also checked that the n = 1 instance of green_82_upper_bound, whose right-hand side is 0 because log 1 = 0, is satisfiable.

(3) Elaboration. n : ℕ and C : ℝ in the variants; (2/3 : ℝ) is a real exponent; cos is Real.cos; a is cast with Int.cast.

(4) Answer slot. green_82 sets answer(sorry) : ℕ+ → ℕ∞ equal to minZeros, i.e. it asks for the exact minimum-zeros function. This is the repository's usual style for 'what is the value' questions (cf. green_51). A trivial filling by minZeros itself is acknowledged in CONTRIBUTING.md and is not a defect.

(5) Status. Green's list dated 2026-01-30 does not mark Problem 82 as solved. The only bounds are (log log n)^{1-o(1)} (Bedert) and O((n log n)^{2/3}) (J-S, Konyagin). Semantic Scholar citations of both papers show no later resolution. So research open (main) and research solved (the two bound variants) are accurate.

(6) Not read directly. I did not read Littlewood's 1968 book; his wording comes from the J-S and Bedert quotations.

(7) Checkout state. The checkout already had a modified lakefile.toml and an untracked run/ directory, both timestamped 12:21, before this review began. I did not create them and modified nothing under /opt/formal-conjectures.
